region: Ovid · Cayuga Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
about: Six Eighty Cellars sits on the steep west shore of Cayuga Lake, near Ovid. Dave and Melissa Pittard of Skaneateles, who also own neighbouring Buttonwood Grove Winery, bought the former Toro Run Winery in 2020 for its established vineyards and opened Six Eighty the following year. The name comes from the land: the slope rises 680 feet from the bottom of the lake to the top of the property. Head winemaker Ian Barry, a Finger Lakes veteran of Heron Hill and Swedish Hill, works with certified-sustainable estate fruit.

The winery is known for raising wines in unusual vessels, from clay eggs and terracotta to sandstone and concrete, and for less common grapes such as Grüner Veltliner, Austria’s signature white. This one comes from the estate’s 89 Block and was made partly in stainless steel and partly in an Italian concrete “tulip”, a tall, tapered fermenter whose shape keeps the lees in gentle motion. The wine then spent nine months on its lees, with regular stirring, which builds texture. It is fully dry, at 11.7% alcohol.

The winery calls the result lush and lively: the concrete and the long contact with the lees give a rounder, smoother feel than steel alone would, while the cool lakeside site keeps the wine crisp. Expect a clean, classic Grüner nose and a smooth palate of citrus and lemongrass. Six Eighty also makes Grüner Veltliner as a pét-nat, a sparkling counterpart to this still bottling.
